body: [A10] Clue from [R370-3](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/604#issuecomment-5860812832) (PR #604): in all three non-stops (talker cycles 13, 24 and 75), the DUT sent its own MRP LeaveAll within 0.1 s of the bridge's Listener `Lv`. The stopping cycles 1-5 show no such coincidence. A LeaveAll timer firing inside the withdrawal window, and re-asserting state that keeps the stream running, is the first hypothesis to test. The records are published at `review-evidence/75-r1/author-r3/talker-013,024,075/msrp.tsv`.

[A10] **Analysis done; the fix is in the processor.** A deterministic SRP-engine simulation reproduces the mechanism. The engine ages its Listener registrar (IN to LV) at LeaveAll timer expiry, before its own LeaveAll is transmitted. A Listener Leave arriving in that window finds LV, does not unregister, and the stream stays active (`hdl/srp/KL_srp_top.sv:1125`, `KL_srp_talker_fsm.sv:564,630,693,698` in the processor). All three bench non-stops, and none of the 97 stops, match that timing. **Donor issue:** Mister-M-alt/protocol-processor-control-plane-avb-milan#127 moves the registrar event to the transmit action. The parent then adopts the pin with a CRF STREAM_STOP regression. **Decision:** LV + rLv semantics stay as documented. A stop target stricter than the table for a genuine LeaveAll cycle would need its own requirement decision, so this issue's acceptance 3 is read as "within one PDU period of a withdrawal that reaches an IN registrar".
